decision: Accepted as offline protocol arithmetic and source-informed design; no native or device qualification

normalized_model.scope: Complete unique final-write occurrences, independent ordered domains, full-row completion and contiguous frontiers, actual tile extents, epoch/ABA rejection, saved-Xe and primary-reader lifetimes, explicit outer hidden/aux/descriptor retirement. The earlier17-check result is retained as history.

online_model.scope: New online issue-order and tile/domain sealing schedules only; the prior18 checks were not rerun or counted as new coverage.

root_review: Read both model implementations and online test schedules. Each expected occurrence has one static source/writer domain; actual submission assigns its sequence in that domain. Duplicate issue is rejected before mutation.

ForwardPeer source-ready polling and cross-source carry in fm_forward.hpp198-291 prove the actual order cannot be fixed from source-major output layout. The two arrival-order schedules produce different sequence mappings while requiring the same final tile contents.

A tile/domain watermark is sealed only after its complete expected occurrence set was issued. Ready requires every expected domain seal and its completion frontier. Earlier completed sources therefore cannot authorize a tile containing unissued later-source rows.

Full-row retirement cannot skip a completion gap; separate QPs remain separate. Compute-ready never authorizes Xe reuse: writes, primary-reader leases, saved backward lifetime and hidden/aux/descriptor outer retirement remain required.

The outer retirement API is an explicit caller assertion, not observed hardware evidence. Epoch transition clears issued orders, seals and outer retirement; old notifications cannot authorize the new epoch.
remaining: Extract and cross-check actual final occurrence/writer metadata from the checked Notify and forwarding structures. Static source/expert counts alone are insufficient.

Map actual issue sequence and full-payload retirement to each local writer or physical ordered QP. Audit both remote payload visibility and seal/frontier publication/acquire before native implementation.
Define distributed expected counts and seal publication without a progress cycle or a blocking source-order workaround. Retain old terminal completion and full Xe storage initially.
Validate native compute component under the separately approved conditional device contract. These CPU models grant no additional deployment, native build or device permission.
